record.coverage_notes: Main text: 'we generated stochastic FLP-based lineage clones that expressed CsChrimson in 12 A neurons in one or a few hemisegment(s)'. The whole-hemilineage driver (unc-4-GAL4DBD, TfAP2-GAL4AD) was lethal, so no adult whole-hemilineage experiment exists.

record.effector: 20XUAS>dsFRT>CsChrimson-mVenus, optogenetic activation (red 620-625 nm or halogen white light, 0.2 mM all-trans retinal)
record.locator: Table 2, row 12 A; Results, 'Hemilineage 12A' section; Figure 6F, 6G; Figure 3-video 36, Figure 3-video 37
record.notes: record_type clonal (FLP-based lineage clones); the clone was also effectively one-sided (one side of T1). d2 = yes from the Figure 6G legend ('its right front leg'); the middle and hind legs are not described. 'a single swing movement' is explicitly single, so d7 = no. Bilateral wing opening gives d11/d12 = yes and Table 2 adds bilateral wing buzzing (d13 = yes).
record.other_observation: Figure 6G: 'The fly folds both wings outward and swings its right front leg forward upon optogenetic activation.'
record.penetrance: We found two cases where optogenetic activation resulted in bilateral wing opening and a leg swing
record.preparation_detail: headless fly; clone in one side of the T1 segment, dissected and immunostained afterwards to identify the clone (Figure 3-video 36, Figure 3-video 37, 100 FPS)
record.quote: Animals expressing CsChrimson in 12 A neurons in one side of the T1 segment showed a single swing movement of the leg

record.other_observation: The backward walking is reported as occurring 'immediately after the stimulus termination', so it is recorded here rather than coded as during-activation walking (d8).

record.coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 'Dr-p65.AD; ey-GAL4-DBD: Somewhat specific and good coverage of 21A neurons in both adult and larval VNCs. A medially located cluster is also labeled, that likely contains 14A neurons.'

record.notes: Second driver line tested on 21A ('Dr-GAL4AD and ey-GAL4DBD'); the text says both lines gave consistent results in intact and decapitated animals, so the decapitated phenotype of Table 2 (flexion of the legs, body lowered and held) is coded here. record_type partial_or_mixed because Supplementary file 1 says this line also labels a cluster that likely contains 14A neurons. The quote joins two sentences of the same paragraph (ellipsis marks the cut).
record.quote: Both combinations target most of the 21 A neurons... Stimulation of either intact or decapitated animals forced the leg segments into a specific geometry.

record.coverage_notes: Results p. 17: the whole-hemilineage driver (unc-4-GAL4DBD, TfAP2-GAL4AD) was lethal with CsChrimson, so 'we generated stochastic FLP-based lineage clones that expressed CsChrimson in 12 A neurons in one or a few hemisegment(s)'. The clones coded here were in one side of the T1 segment.
record.driver: TfAP-2-GAL4 with heat-shock FLP-based lineage clones (20XUAS>dsFRT>CsChrimson-mVenus in attp18, pBPhsFlp2::PEST in attp3)

record.notes: The front leg identification comes from the Figure 6 legend ('right front leg'), which codes d2; the source does not report middle or hind leg movement, so d3 and d4 are not_assessed. A single swing is not repeated (d7 'no') and the Figure 6 legend calls it 'single-step behavior', which is not coordinated walking (d8 'no'). Bilateral wing opening codes d11 and d12; Table 2 reports bilateral wing buzzing, which codes d13. The whole-hemilineage line unc-4-GAL4DBD/TfAP2-GAL4AD gave no surviving adults, so it yields no record.
record.other_observation: Figure 6 legend: 'The fly folds both wings outward and swings its right front leg forward upon optogenetic activation.' record.coverage_notes: Results p. 17: 'We also observed the following behavioral phenotypes in response to optogenetic activation, but we did not dissect the animals to further identify the lineage clone'. The extent and location of the clones in these animals is therefore unknown.
record.driver: TfAP-2-GAL4 with heat-shock FLP-based lineage clones (20XUAS>dsFRT>CsChrimson-mVenus in attp18, pBPhsFlp2::PEST in attp3); clones not identified by dissection
record.notes: Separate record from 0036 because these are different clone-bearing animals whose clones were not identified. Per protocol section 2, the after-effect (backward walking) is kept out of the coded dimensions.
record.other_observation: Backward walking occurred immediately after the stimulus ended, not during activation, so it is reported here rather than coded in d8.
record.quote: high frequency wing beating, backward walking immediately after the stimulus termination, and abdominal extension and bending
